task:
BUILD PART A OF 4 OF F2D PR4 (governed operator actions): the pinned operator-code identity, the complete-read calibration action, and the histogram converter. Base on current origin/main (record the SHA; it must include F2d PR3, merged as #811 at af4817793170d522c0e5c1104441bb2eb1f34fb5). New branch, no target_branch. Parts B (capacity gate + measurement workflow), C (build actions + lifecycle status) and D (publish action + plan probe + release gate) will update this same branch later; leave it in a state a follow-up can continue from. No pull request is opened until all four parts have landed.

AUTHORITY: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f2d-wide-archetype-and-product-attachment-design.md. Read CLAUDE.md first, then design sections 8.2 (calibration and the complete read), 8.3 (pinned code identities -- implement all of it in this part), 8.4 only the "Histogram conversion" paragraph, and the PR4 bullet in section 10. Read also the existing governed actions you will model on: scripts/operator/actions/v3-archetype-calibration-probe.sh (the detached read-only probe: pinned host/FQDN/container/database constants, require_target, the docker run of the API image with the repo bind-mounted read-only at /work, the offline psycopg wheelhouse at .v3-probe-wheelhouse, the 1500 s timeout, the receipt on stdout), scripts/operator/actions/v3-system-search-f1.sh (the start/status pattern: STATE_ROOT, worker container label, sealed receipt file, status that only reads), scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-lifecycle-status.sh (the operation-result JSON envelope: schema_version, operation, status, failures, read_only, db_writes_performed), scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py (scores through score_raw_system since PR1 part 3), and the probe's wiring in .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml (the operation allowlist choice list AND the case statement around line 83 must both be extended; the f1-start step shows how a wheelhouse is downloaded and the trusted-main tree is staged over SSH). Where this task and the design differ, the design wins; where the design and the current code differ, follow the design and name the conflict in your summary. Everything here is code only: no deployment, no production access, no production credentials. The actions you write are not run in this PR; the owner dispatches them later through the governed workflow.

ALLOWED FILES: deploy/v3-production/f2d-operator-code.txt (new); scripts/operator/lib/f2d_operator_identity.sh (new, shared shell helper) and scripts/operator/lib/f2d_operator_identity.py (new, the same computation in Python for in-container use); scripts/operator/actions/v3-archetype-calibration-complete.sh (new); scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_complete.py (new, the in-container complete read; may import from scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py); scripts/dev/convert_calibration_histogram.py (new); .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml (allowlist choice list, case statement, and the start/status/upload steps for the new action, modelled on the f1 and probe steps); tests/test_f2d_operator_identity.py (new), tests/test_v3_archetype_calibration_complete.py (new), tests/test_convert_calibration_histogram.py (new), whichever existing tests assert the chatgpt-ed-new-ops workflow allowlist/schema (grep tests/ for chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml; extend them); tests/test_python314_execution_surfaces.py only if new Python entry points must be listed; CHANGES.md. Any other changed path must be justified in your summary as required by a specific failing test, otherwise it is a failure.

OPERATOR-CODE MANIFEST AND IDENTITY (design 8.3). deploy/v3-production/f2d-operator-code.txt lists, one repository-relative path per line (sorted, no duplicates, comments allowed with #), every file the F2d operator path executes: scripts/operator/actions/v3-archetype-calibration-complete.sh and the F2d actions parts B-D will add (list them now with their planned names so the manifest is complete when they land: scripts/operator/actions/v3-finder-capacity-gate.sh, scripts/operator/actions/v3-system-search-f1.sh, scripts/operator/actions/v3-system-archetype.sh, scripts/operator/actions/v3-publish-derived-products.sh, scripts/operator/actions/v3-archetype-plan-probe.sh -- a listed path that does not exist yet makes the identity computation REFUSE, so for this part list only the files that exist and leave a clearly marked comment block naming the parts B-D files to be appended when they land), the shared shell helpers they source (scripts/operator/lib/ is new in this part; scripts/operator/protected_resources.sh if any F2d action sources it), scripts/v3_system_search.py, scripts/v3_system_search_parallel.py, scripts/v3_system_archetype.py, shared_contracts/v3_system_archetype_model.py and its re-export scripts/v3_system_archetype_model.py, scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_probe.py, scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_complete.py, scripts/dev/measure_wide_archetype_footprint.py, scripts/dev/convert_calibration_histogram.py, the exact psycopg requirement string the complete read installs (record it as a line of the form requirement:psycopg[binary]==3.3.4 and have the identity include that string verbatim), and the manifest file itself. f2d_operator_code_sha256 = SHA-256 of the canonical JSON list of [path, file_sha256] pairs over every listed path (sorted by path; compact separators; the manifest's own entry included; a requirement line contributes [the requirement line, sha256 of its text]). Both helpers compute it identically (a test proves shell and Python agree byte for byte on the committed tree and on a tree with one listed file changed), and both REFUSE (non-zero, named reason) when a listed path is missing, unreadable, or a symlink, or when the attested value is missing or malformed. The check contract for every F2d action: compute over its own checkout BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE and compare with the attested value passed in (an environment variable or argument the workflow supplies from the release attestation; part D wires the attestation field -- for now the actions read F2D_OPERATOR_CODE_SHA256_ATTESTED and refuse when it is unset or different). Tests: a checkout with any manifest-listed file changed is refused; a change to an unlisted file (a docs file) does not move the identity; a missing listed path refuses; a symlinked listed path refuses; shell and Python agree.

COMPLETE READ ACTION (design 8.2). scripts/operator/actions/v3-archetype-calibration-complete.sh with start and status modes, modelled on the probe and f1 actions: the same pinned TARGET_HOSTNAME/TARGET_FQDN/POSTGRES_CONTAINER/DATABASE_USER/DATABASE_NAME/WORKER_NETWORK constants and require_target; target generation ratings_v4_prod_p4_parallel_v1 pinned by key AND by the expected generation UUID/publication sequence read from the step 0 receipt (docs/operations/evidence/2026-10-10-v3-derived-lifecycle-status-receipt.json -- read the values from the file at build time into constants, do not fetch at run time); identity check first (F2D_OPERATOR_CODE_SHA256_ATTESTED); read-only: the worker container gets the API image, the repo bind-mounted read-only at /work, the offline wheelhouse, --read-only, resource bounds, and a DATABASE_URL via env file exactly as the probe does; it is DETACHED (start returns after launching the named worker container with the operation label; status reads the container state and the checkpoint/receipt files under STATE_ROOT and never mutates). The in-container program scripts/v3_archetype_calibration_complete.py scores EVERY system of the generation through score_raw_system via the model's two shared SQL constants (per canonical chunk ordinal, in chunk order), checkpoints after each chunk to a file under a writable tmpfs-backed state path mounted from STATE_ROOT so a restart resumes from the last complete chunk (start detects an existing checkpoint for the same generation UUID + identity and resumes; a checkpoint for a different generation or identity is refused, not overwritten), and on completion writes a sealed receipt (JSON with content_sha256 over its canonical body) containing: mode: complete; the generation key/UUID/publication sequence; system_count; per-key tier counts (S/A/B/C/D) in total AND per canonical chunk ordinal with the chunk plan identity (the ordered list of chunk ordinals and their row counts, hashed); coefficients and code_identity as the probe records them; archetype_model_sha256 and model_file_sha256; f2d_operator_code_sha256 of the checkout; the EXPECTED PRODUCT MANIFEST that scripts/v3_system_archetype.product_manifest() produces for this generation and this code (computed, not read from a row -- the product is not registered yet) and its manifest sha256; and sigma_all = the sum over the eight keys of (S+A+B)/total + (S+A)/total + S/total. Inside the container it also refuses, before scoring, if any imported module whose file lies under /work is not a manifest-listed path (walk sys.modules after imports). It never writes a product row (assert in a test that the program's source contains no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE and opens its connection read-only / default_transaction_read_only). Per-key totals must equal system_count (assert before sealing; otherwise write a failure receipt and exit non-zero). Workflow: add v3-archetype-calibration-complete-start and v3-archetype-calibration-complete-status to the choice list, the case statement, and start/status/upload steps modelled on the f1 pair (wheelhouse download of psycopg[binary]==3.3.4, stage trusted-main, root-or-sudo launch, receipt artifact upload). Tests (disposable PostgreSQL 18 through the existing archetype fixtures where a database is needed; runners have no PostgreSQL, so write them, run what runs without a database, and list the rest): start/status contract (status is read-only; start refuses without the attested identity; start refuses a checkpoint for another generation); a restart resumes from the checkpoint and the final receipt equals a fresh run's; per-key totals equal the system count and sigma_all equals the sum of the 24 fractions; per-chunk counts sum to the totals; the receipt's expected manifest equals product_manifest() for the fixture generation; the in-container module-outside-manifest refusal; the probe test's existing assertion that no product rows are written extends to the complete read; the sampled probe's receipt (mode absent or not 'complete') is distinguishable from the complete receipt by a validator function the gate (part B) will import.

HISTOGRAM CONVERTER (design 8.4 "Histogram conversion"). scripts/dev/convert_calibration_histogram.py takes a complete-read receipt and writes the fractions JSON {<key>: {"60": f, "76": f, "88": f}} the footprint script's --fractions-json consumes (that script exists since PR1 part 3): per key total = S+A+B+C+D; f["88"] = S/total; f["76"] = (S+A)/total; f["60"] = (S+A+B)/total; it asserts f60 >= f76 >= f88, every one of the eight keys present, each total equal to the receipt's recorded system_count, refuses a receipt whose mode is not 'complete' or whose content_sha256 does not verify, and writes beside the fractions: fractions_sha256 (canonical JSON digest of the fractions object), the source receipt's content_sha256, its f2d_operator_code_sha256, and the converter's own f2d_operator_code_sha256 of the checkout (so the gate can refuse a fractions file the converter did not produce). Pure stdlib. Tests: the arithmetic on a hand-built receipt; the monotonic assertion; missing key; total mismatch; non-complete mode refused; bad seal refused; output digest stable.

VALIDATION TO RUN AND REPORT WITH EXACT COUNTS: bash -n on every new shell file; ruff check scripts tests; python -m pytest tests/test_f2d_operator_identity.py tests/test_convert_calibration_histogram.py tests/test_python314_execution_surfaces.py -q -p no:warnings plus the ops-workflow contract test and every touched module that runs without a database; the shell and Python identity values printed for the committed tree (they must be equal). Parameterized SQL only; fail-closed; keep secrets off command lines (DSN via env file as the probe does).

IF YOU CANNOT FINISH EVERYTHING IN THIS SESSION, complete in this order and stop cleanly: manifest + identity helpers + their tests; converter + tests; complete-read program; complete-read action + workflow wiring; remaining tests. State precisely what remains so part B can begin. End with: files changed; tests run with counts; database tests written but not run; the identity value for the committed tree; and any design-versus-code conflict you found.
